title: "Search and ranking"
subtitle: "A search over edits ordered by a ranker and a value estimate, measured in calls to the local solver."
---

::: {.callout-note title="Status"}
Built and run. Given the indirect lift's formation sequence, the search
realizes the lift from rest at μ = 0.3, 0.4 and 0.5
([Results](../results/index.qmd)). Finding that sequence from the scene alone
is open and is the next work: rebuild the value 𝒱₀ for the current gate, then
train a learned value V₁ by expert iteration with exploration
([Issues](issues.qmd)).
:::

## The search

A node is a simulated state, identified by its formation, the disk's
connected region and the box's pose within a 10 mm test radius, merged only
when the gate's verdicts agree ([Node identity](node-identity.qmd)). From a node, the candidates are
the edits that pass [the hold gate](hold-gate.qmd); each expansion calls the
[local solver](local-solver.qmd) Λ, which is the expensive part. The search
is policy-guided heuristic search (PHS\*, Orseau and Lelis 2021): a ranker
gives a probability π to each candidate edit, nodes are expanded in order of
a key built from their depth, the probability of their path and a heuristic
factor η from a value estimate, Λ is charged when a node is expanded, and
edits the gate rejects get π = 0. For this order the number of expansions is
bounded by the depth and probability of the solution, scaled by η. The
theory note extends the bound to duplicate states (with the safe duplicate
rule and the node key of [Node identity](node-identity.qmd)), to a Λ that
fails at random (with restarts), and to nodes popped in batches.

## The search's actions and acceptance {#design}

- **Outcome children.** A call yields at most one child, labelled by the
  state it actually reaches. The child is accepted if it is the requested
  state, or if it lowers the value estimate by at least δ = 10 mm, the
  merge test radius of [Node identity](node-identity.qmd). A call that does not end in the requested
  formation can still leave the box where a short route continues.
- **Box transports.** Besides the edits, the box can be moved *within* its
  contact state, with its own gate: a box move is refused when no disk
  placement on the face can push the box along the planned path (a linear
  program at five poses). The push to the goal aims at the goal window's
  centre.
- **Releases are off.** Release edits (let the box go and let it come to
  rest in the next state) are in the code but not part of the method: the
  method's lift is held at every instant.
- **The order** is PHS\* with its heuristic factor η from a value function,
  clipped to [1, η<sub>max</sub>], η<sub>max</sub> = 10. The ranker is uniform
  over the legal edits for now.
- **The value.** 𝒱₀: the distance to the goal in the edit graph plus the
  box's distance to a fixed set of poses where the next edit passes the gate.
  To follow: a learned value V₁, the expected number of Λ calls to the goal,
  trained by expert iteration with exploration on every logged call, failures
  included (a call that succeeds with probability p costs about 1/p calls);
  the distance to the goal enters only as shaping and as an input.
- **Which ends count.** An end with the disk outside its workspace (the
  joint ranges) is invalid; quasi-static runs reject ends reached through a
  dynamic event.
- **No gap screen, no retries.** No distance screen filters the candidates
  (the gate and box transport decide; distance only orders them); the
  disk's clearance check is part of the gate. The planner and every reported
  result use no retries. The approach to an edit lasts as long as its path
  needs. The settle clause of the success test is off for formation edits and
  required for the final goal state.

## The ranker

*The planned architecture. The ranker in the reported runs is uniform; the
attention ranker comes after the search has held solves to train on.*

- **Inputs:** one token per contact template (type, gap, normal,
  contact-set length, whether it is on), one per body, and one for the goal;
  attention across tokens, with learned biases for pairs that are related by
  containment or share a body or an environment element.
- **Output:** a score per candidate edit, normalized over the candidates into
  π.
- **Training:** supervised, from searches that call Λ without guidance on
  many scene instances: the policy-guided-search loss on solution paths, plus
  a cross-entropy on whether each Λ call succeeded.
- **Baselines:** search without guidance; the gate's margin as the score; and
  a learned feasibility classifier with uniform-cost search on −Σ ln P
  (Hauser, Bretl and Latombe, ICRA 2005).

## Scene families

| Family | Scene and goal |
|---|---|
| F1. Step, randomized | step height, box size, friction, starts; goals on the platform; also lowering the box from the platform |
| F2. Staircase | two or three steps of random rise and tread |
| F3. Wall and ledge | topple the box against a wall, or lift it onto a ledge beside it |

One disk for now. The families come after the search finds the indirect lift
on the step unhinted, and a second disk after that. Validity is computed from
the geometry for each family ([Contact states](contact-states.qmd#validity)).

**The validity tables for all three families.** The builder
now takes any polygonal environment and a rectangular box. It reproduces the
step's tables exactly, and built the two new families (default dimensions;
random-instance ranges are documented, not yet sampled):

| | Step | F2 staircase (2 steps) | F3 wall and ledge |
|---|---|---|---|
| Certified valid formations | 357 | 649 | 473 |
| Nodes of W (recognizable, vertex–vertex only alone) | 328 | 592 | 443 |
| Excluded sets | 560 pairs + 1 triple | 1,624 pairs + 5 triples | 840 pairs + 10 triples |
| Compound edges (local rule, ρ = 25 mm) | 92 | 172 | 144 |

New in the families: concave corners the box can wedge into (80 staircase
formations, 42 wall-and-ledge), and pivot-like compound edges at every convex
corner. Neither has collinear edges, so the "pit" case of the theory note
doesn't arise yet.

**The test:** a 2 × 2 table of transfer, holding out an environment family
(F3) and holding out the number of disks (once a second disk is built), with cost measured in Λ calls. A
targeted literature search found learned guidance for contact or mode search
tested on held-out instances, objects, object counts or robot counts, but
not on a held-out family of environments; the closest work counts solver
calls with learned feasibility for pick-and-place (Ortiz-Haro et al., ICRA
2023).
